one_liner: Low-level D binding to Linux io_uring (no liburing); author's echo and HTTP microbenchmarks edge C liburing servers.
what_it_does: during is a thin D wrapper over the io_uring syscalls: it sets up and mmaps the rings itself, exposes the submission queue as an output range and the completion queue as an input range, and offers prepXX helpers (prepReadFixed, prepRecv, prepAccept, prepProvideBuffers, prepSendZc, ...) that fill SubmissionEntry structs in place. It is neither an event loop nor an HTTP server; you write the loop yourself. It runs with druntime or under -betterC, is @nogc nothrow, and 0.5.0/0.6.0 claim opcode and register-opcode parity with Linux 7.1-rc4 and liburing 2.9. For D programs it replaces liburing; it does not replace any C or C++ server.
how_it_is_fast: There is no new algorithm: speed comes from io_uring itself (one ring shared with the kernel, registered fixed buffers via IORING_REGISTER_BUFFERS, kernel-selected provided buffers, FAST_POLL, multishot ops) plus a wrapper with no hot-path overhead: put/putWith fill SQEs directly in the mapped ring, wait() skips io_uring_enter when completions are already queued, and nothing allocates. The echo example preallocates a registered buffer pool and swaps read/write buffers per client; the httpbench responder is a near line-by-line port of the C liburing server, so any gap there reflects the wrapper versus liburing plus compiler flags, not a different design.
when_to_use: D code (LDC, DMD or GDC) on Linux that needs direct io_uring access in @nogc/nothrow or -betterC code without linking the C liburing.
Building your own D event loop or runtime that wants recent io_uring features (provided-buffer rings, multishot accept/recv, SEND_ZC, NAPI, ring resize) with liburing-2.9-level coverage.
Single-core socket responders or proxies where syscall count per request dominates and you can batch several SQEs per io_uring_enter, as the httpbench port does.
Code that must choose a path at runtime by kernel version: Uring.probe() reports which opcodes the running kernel supports.
when_not_to_use: C or C++ projects: liburing is the native equivalent and during adds nothing algorithmic over it.
When you want a server or a ready event loop: during has neither; the HttpArena siblings (libxev, tokio-uring, nginx-class C servers) are complete stacks.
Non-Linux targets or old kernels: dub.sdl declares platforms "linux", most networking ops need 5.5 to 5.7+, and the httpbench io_uring servers refuse to start without FAST_POLL (5.7+).
Containers or users with a low RLIMIT_MEMLOCK: every ring and registered buffer counts against memlock; the README warns the tests and the echo example can fail to initialise.
Expecting the README's 2.9x echo speedup today: those numbers come from a 2019 kernel whose socket I/O path for io_uring no longer exists and were not re-measured.

integration.form: dub package (source library, builds a static lib); optional Meson build
integration.dependencies: none at runtime (no liburing, druntime optional under betterC); the test runner uses silly and the echo example uses mempooled
integration.min_toolchain: CI matrix DMD 2.091.1 and LDC 1.24.0 up to latest; CHANGELOG 0.5.0 says the suite passes on LDC 1.21+ (frontend 2.091+); betterC tests build with DMD 2.098
integration.platforms: Linux only (CI on ubuntu-latest x86-64); features gated by the running kernel
integration.thread_safety: not documented; Uring is a handle with a non-atomic reference count (refs++ in the copy constructor), so use one ring per thread
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — replaces liburing for D code (similar prep helpers and opcode coverage), not the C/C++ echo or HTTP servers it was compared with

gotchas: Harness flaw, echo numbers not reproducible: the first published echo results (commit e12d12c, 2019-12-07) were during 88,348 vs C++ epoll 79,820 req/s (1.11x); the next day's README-only commit acc79a4 ('benchmark update') reports epoll 45,063 (-44%) and during 131,090 (+48%) and adds mrloop, with app.d unchanged and only CI, Makefile and README commits in between. The 2.91x headline therefore swung from 1.11x between two of the author's own runs of the same code.

Harness flaw, kernel artifact: on the stated kernel 5.3.12, io_prep_rw marks every socket READ_FIXED/WRITE_FIXED REQ_F_MUST_PUNT (sockets fail io_file_supports_async) and queues it on the io_ring-wq workqueue (max_active min(sq_entries-1, 2 x CPUs), 32 on the 16-thread 3700X); the echo server's accept()ed sockets are blocking (accept passes flags 0), so each pending read parks a kernel worker in recv. The 'single threaded' during server thus did its socket I/O on up to 32 kernel threads, while the C++ epoll baseline (edge-triggered, reads until EAGAIN, so at least read, read, write and epoll_wait per echo; its own Makefile uses -O2 -g) does every syscall on one thread and mrloop polls first (POLL_ADD, then READV, then WRITEV per echo). The comparison measures 2019 io_uring punting, not D or the wrapper, and does not carry over to 5.7+ kernels.

The echo example is a benchmark toy: onWrite ignores the write result (short writes and errors are dropped), and a failed read's negative res is stored as lastRead and reused as the next write length.

httpbench pairs are close to same-code but not same-build: the D port uses 1024-byte provided buffers vs C 2048 and adds --mcpu=native --ffast-math to ldc2 while gcc gets plain -O3; both abort on a partial request ('FIXME: partial request handling not implemented'), and each cell is one 30 s run on a 2-vCPU KVM guest, where the README also notes an io_uring regression from kernel 5.7.16.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: The siblings are complete servers (HttpArena entries such as libxev, tokio-uring, nginx-class C servers) or the same author's D epoll port in httpbench; pick during only when you write D and want raw io_uring control without liburing, and pick libxev (Zig) or tokio-uring (Rust) when you want a ready io_uring event loop in those languages.
verified_claims_summary: In December 2019 the author measured a single-threaded during echo server at 131,090 req/s vs mrloop (C, liburing, -O3) 95,894 and methane's C++ epoll server 45,063 (rust_echo_bench, 50 clients, 512 B, 10 s, best of 3, Ryzen 7 3700X, Fedora 31 kernel 5.3.12, ldc2 1.18.0); these are different programs and a run one day earlier showed only 1.11x over epoll. In httpbench (Fedora 36 host, ldc2 1.29.0 vs gcc -O3, server in a 2-vCPU KVM guest, wrk 4.1.0) a D port of the C liburing HTTP responder ran at 0.97x to 1.20x of the C original in single 30 s runs.
status_note: Active (0.6.0 released 2026-10-09 with Linux 7.1-rc4 opcode parity, BSL-1.0, 37 stars) and usable as a dub dependency, but its only performance evidence is the 2019 echo run and the httpbench port, neither re-measured on the rewritten library, and the echo comparison is a kernel-punting artifact.
